title: improv·artist · atmospheric (Mark Rothko)
mutation_directive: improv artist: atmospheric via Mark Rothko

improv_extras.practice: color fields that vibrate; contemplative; soft rectangles bleeding into ground

v1.feedback: Differential growth as the boundary mechanism between color fields is a genuinely smart mapping — the idea clearly drove the design, not just the palette. However, AdditiveBlending is the wrong compositing mode for Rothko: his paintings absorb light, they don't emit it. Switch to NormalBlending with higher base alpha and layered opacity falloff to get that matte, soaked-into-canvas density. The breathing vertex displacement is too uniform — Rothko's fields shift color temperature across their area, so modulate the color hue/saturation spatially (warmer center, cooler edges) rather than just pulsing luminosity globally.

v2.feedback: The Rothko concept lands well — three differential-growth curves as band boundaries is a smart structural choice, and NormalBlending gives the matte, pigment-soaked density the brief demands. The warm-center/cool-edge spatial modulation is a genuine design decision driven by the idea. Two things to refine: the differential growth curves are doing mechanical work (defining boundaries) but their organic undulation isn't visually legible as a Rothko soft-edge — consider rendering the boundary zone itself as a wider gradient bleed rather than a hard curve-to-curve fill, so the color transitions feel more like paint soaking into raw canvas. Second, 40k particles at this camera distance risk reading as flat matte rectangles rather than luminous fields — Rothko's power is in the optical flicker at edges, so concentrate more particle density and subtle color variance right at the boundary zones where bands meet.
